title: Final Multi-Concept Foundations Project
learningObjectives: Describe the purpose and scope of final multi-concept foundations project.
Plan the required data, inputs, outputs, and behaviors.
Break the solution into manageable functions or steps.
Implement and test normal, invalid, and boundary cases.
Review the result and explain limitations and improvements.

understand.concept: A final foundations project combines multiple programming concepts into a small, complete solution. Learners should choose a problem, define scope, plan data, decompose behavior, implement, validate, test, document, and review. A successful project is not measured only by feature count; it should be understandable, correct for its scope, and responsibly designed.
understand.whyItMatters: Integration practice reveals how foundational ideas work together and gives learners evidence of independent problem-solving.
understand.analogy: Think of completing a small real-world task by defining the goal, organizing the work, checking each step, and reviewing the finished result.
understand.analogyLimit: Software projects require precise requirements, data and code design, technical testing, and iterative change; the analogy only introduces a workflow.

explain.narrative:
A final foundations project combines multiple programming concepts into a small, complete solution. Learners should choose a problem, define scope, plan data, decompose behavior, implement, validate, test, document, and review. A successful project is not measured only by feature count; it should be understandable, correct for its scope, and responsibly designed.

Build incrementally and keep the project scope appropriate for your current skills. The examples illustrate individual design steps; they are not a complete ready-made project. Test your own implementation and document assumptions.

commonMistakes: Starting implementation without defining scope or acceptance criteria.
Combining input, logic, and display in one tangled block.
Claiming features or data persist when they are only in memory.
Adding features before the core workflow works and is tested.

guidedTask.title: Guided Project
guidedTask.instructions: Choose a manageable app (quiz, records, or utility). Write a problem statement, requirements, data shape, function/module plan, test cases, and a first working version. Review scope before adding features.
steps: Choose a manageable app (quiz, records, or utility). Write a problem statement, requirements, data shape, function/module plan, test cases, and a first working version. Review scope before adding features.
Write a short scope and acceptance checklist.
Test a normal case and at least two edge/error cases.

independentTask.title: Independent Project
independentTask.instructions: Build an original small application using at least collections, functions, decisions, loops, input validation, error handling, tests, documentation, and a safe data policy. Include a design sketch, test evidence, limitations, and a short retrospective.
requirements: Keep the project original and appropriately scoped.
